---
title: "O5 Dimensionality — Bayesian crossed random-effects IRT"
format: html
params:
  language_a: "English (American)"
  language_b: "Spanish (Mexican)"
  min_items_per_child: 20   # per administration
  thin_items: 1           # keep every k-th item/language; full EN-SP is ~1665 items
  admins: "all"           # "all" administrations (child ability shared across visits) | "latest" per child x language
  age_spline_df: 3        # natural-spline df for the age effect on ability (1 = linear)
  fit_models: false
  method: "sample"        # "sample" (NUTS). ADVI/pathfinder are unreliable here — see below.
  link_concepts: "auto"   # "auto" | TRUE | FALSE — TE linking only helps with lots of overlap
---

::: {.callout-important}
**Use NUTS, not ADVI.** On the real EN–SP data (474 children) rstan's meanfield
VB diverged completely — ELBO oscillating, `rho`/`ecv`/`lambda_g` collapsing to 0.
NUTS on the same model is well-behaved (0 divergences, coherent posterior). The
mirt route in `08` also fails to converge on this sample. This file is the one
that produces a trustworthy number, at the cost of a multi-hour run.
:::

# Idea

Rather than let differential exposure masquerade as a factor (as an exploratory
mIRT would), model it, and turn the dimensionality question into a
**variance-components** question:

- item easiness = translation-equivalent **concept** term (shared by `dog` /
  `perro` via `uni_lemma`) + **language-specific offset** (auto-collapsed to one
  flat item level when too few items link across languages);
- child ability across the `L` languages is `MVN(0, Sigma)` with a
  **compound-symmetric** covariance — a common `c_shared` between every language
  pair, plus a per-language specific variance `sigma_s[L]^2` on the diagonal;
- exposure + age enter as fixed per-language effects, both taken from each
  **administration's own record** (see *Repeated administrations* below).

Then

- `sigma_s -> 0`   ⇒ unidimensional  (`rho -> 1`)
- `c_shared -> 0`  ⇒ independent lexicons (`rho -> 0`)
- both free        ⇒ estimate `rho` (pairwise) and `ECV` directly — continuous.

The covariance is parameterised through its Cholesky factor rather than a
general loading `lambda_g` multiplying a shared latent, so when the shared part
vanishes (`c_shared -> 0`) there is **no funnel** — the earlier
`lambda_g * theta_g` form sampled fine for the English–Spanish pairs (where
`lambda_g` ≈ 1.9, far from 0) but funnelled badly on the Malaysian trilingual
sample, where the shared dimension really is near zero. `lambda_g` is still
reported (`= sqrt(c_shared)`) for continuity.

`models/bilingual_dim_irt.stan` implements all three hypotheses via the data
flags `estimate_general` / `estimate_specific`, for any number of languages
`L >= 2` (it is a crossed random-effects generalisation of the old concept/word
IRT in `archive/models/model1.stan`).

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(glue)
library(here)
library(cmdstanr)
library(posterior)
library(loo)
library(tidyverse)

source(here("scripts", "dim_irt_helpers.R"))

theme_set(
  theme_bw() +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
          strip.background = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "bottom")
)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

# Data prep (shares helpers with `08_o5_dimensionality_mirt.qmd`)

## Repeated administrations

Most EN–SP children come from longitudinal studies (Hoff, Marchman,
Marchman_BTL, Weisleder): 1749 administrations from 474 children, ages 15–41
months, up to 11 visits per child. An earlier version of this pipeline collapsed
each child's visits into one "ever produced" row (`max()` over administrations)
and paired it with a single child-level age (the first exposure record's,
median-imputed where missing) — which wiped out the age signal entirely
(cor(age, proportion produced) = 0.01; per-administration it is 0.47) and so
mis-specified `beta_age` / `beta_age_exp`.

Now `build_pair_long()` keeps one row per (child, administration, item), each
with its own administration's age and exposure record, and the model treats
repeated visits as:

- **child-level ability** `theta_child[i, l]` (the MVN with `c_shared` /
  `sigma_s` that defines `rho` / `ECV`) shared across all of a child's visits —
  so `rho` is the correlation of children's *stable* language abilities, net of
  the population age curve;
- a **per-administration deviation** `sigma_admin[l] * z_admin[a]`
  (`estimate_admin`, on automatically when visits repeat) absorbing
  visit-to-visit departures from that curve (growth-rate differences, the
  occasion) that would otherwise be local dependence among a visit's items.

`params$admins = "latest"` instead keeps one administration per child x language
(the oldest) — the cross-sectional design the model originally assumed, with the
age now correct.

```{r}
langs <- c(params$language_a, params$language_b)

item_table <- build_item_table(
  items       = readRDS(here("data", "items.rds")),
  instruments = load_instruments()
)
df_demogs <- readRDS(here("data", "demographics.rds"))

# screen the sample FIRST: a language where many children are at the vocabulary
# floor, or where few have an exposure record, cannot support this analysis
# (rho gets attenuated toward 0 by measurement, not by structure)
sample_health(item_table, df_demogs, langs)

# long form the Stan model wants: one row per (child, administration, item),
# each with that administration's age
long <- build_pair_long(
  item_table, df_demogs, langs, admins = params$admins,
  min_items_per_admin = params$min_items_per_child
)

if (params$thin_items > 1) {
  keep_uid <- long$item_lookup |> group_by(language) |>
    filter(row_number() %% params$thin_items == 0) |> pull(uid)
  long$obs <- long$obs |> filter(uid %in% keep_uid)
}

obs <- long$obs
exposure <- admin_language_exposure(df_demogs, langs)   # per-administration records

# sanity check: vocabulary should rise with age within each administration set
obs |> group_by(admin_id, age) |> summarise(prop = mean(y), .groups = "drop") |>
  summarise(cor_age_vocab = cor(age, prop))

link <- if (identical(params$link_concepts, "auto")) NA else
          as.integer(isTRUE(params$link_concepts))

prep <- build_dim_irt_stan_data(
  obs, exposure, langs,
  estimate_general = 1L, estimate_specific = 1L,
  link_concepts = link, age_spline_df = params$age_spline_df, compute_loglik = 1L
)
str(prep$data[c("N", "I", "J", "C", "A", "K_age", "link_concepts", "estimate_admin")])
```

# Fit the three nested variants

Runtime scales with item count. Rough NUTS cost (4 chains, 1000+1000): ~1 h at
150 items, ~3–4 h at 400, 8 h+ at the full 1665. Prototype with
`thin_items: 4`; do the headline run unthinned overnight. The variance
components (`sigma_delta`, `sigma_s`) mix slowest — watch their `rhat` / `ess`.

```{r fit, eval=params$fit_models}
mod <- cmdstan_model(here("models", "bilingual_dim_irt.stan"))

run_variant <- function(g, s, tag) {
  d <- modifyList(prep$data, list(estimate_general = g, estimate_specific = s))
  fit <- mod$sample(data = d, seed = 123, chains = 4, parallel_chains = 4,
                    iter_warmup = 1000, iter_sampling = 1000,
                    adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12)
  fit$save_object(here("models", glue("o5_bayes_{tag}_{make.names(params$language_a)}.rds")))
  print(fit$diagnostic_summary())
  fit
}

fit_full <- run_variant(1, 1, "full")      # general + specific  -> rho, ecv
fit_uni  <- run_variant(1, 0, "unidim")    # sigma_s == 0        -> nested null
fit_two  <- run_variant(0, 1, "twolex")    # lambda_g == 0       -> nested null
```

::: {.callout-warning}
**Corrected 2026-10.** The result below was computed on collapsed visits with
no usable age signal (see *Repeated administrations* above). Refit with each
child's latest administration and its own age (543 items, 948 administrations,
rstan via `scripts/fit_dim_irt.R latest 3`, 0 divergences): **`rho` = `ecv` =
0.40 [0.32, 0.47]**, `c_shared` 1.65 (was 3.4), `sigma_s` 1.64 / 1.52; the age
curve is now monotone (−1.1 logits at 18 vs. 24 months, +1.9 at 30), and
`beta_exp` is unchanged (5.3 / 4.0). Age-driven growth had been loading on the
shared factor. The all-administrations fit (`scripts/fit_dim_irt.R all 3`;
1749 administrations, 0 divergences) gives a stable-ability **`rho` = 0.63
[0.53, 0.72]**, with large per-visit deviations (`sigma_admin` 1.29 / 1.20).
The correlation it implies for a single visit, 0.39 [0.32, 0.45], matches the
latest-administration fit. Saved: `models/o5_bayes_EN-SP-latest-thin3_summary.csv`,
`models/o5_bayes_EN-SP-all-thin3_summary.csv`,
`models/o5_bayes_EN-SP_longitudinal_comparison.csv`.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
**Superseded — result, EN (American) × ES (Mexican), 474 children, 554 items** (thinned 1-in-3
from 1665; `link_concepts = 0`; 4 chains × 1000, 0 divergences, `rho`/`ecv`
`n_eff` ≈ 1300, `rhat` = 1.00):

| quantity | median | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|
| `rho`  (cross-language ability correlation) | **0.585** | 0.519–0.642 |
| `ecv`  (person-level explained common variance) | **0.582** | 0.515–0.640 |
| `lambda_g` | 1.85 | 1.67–2.03 |
| `sigma_s` (EN / ES specific SD) | 1.74 / 1.37 | — |

A **strong common lexical-ability dimension (~58% of reliable person variance)
plus substantial, genuinely language-specific ability (~40%)**. The posterior
excludes both `rho`→1 (single dimension) and `rho`→0 (independent lexicons); the
`unidim` and `twolex` nested fits are not credible. `beta_exp` ≈ 5 / 3.5
(exposure strongly shifts which language's words a child produces).

Follow-ups since done (see *Cross-pair replication* and *SBC calibration*
below): SBC shows the model does not over-state `rho`; the full 1665-item fit
(concept linking on) and an age spline both leave `rho` at ~0.58; and Norwegian
× Polish replicates the ~0.6 estimate in a non-English pair.

Saved: `models/o5_bayes_EN-SP_summary.csv`, `models/o5_bayes_EN-SP-full_summary.csv`.
:::

```{r}
rd <- \(tag) readRDS(here("models", glue("o5_bayes_{tag}_{make.names(params$language_a)}.rds")))
fit_full <- rd("full"); fit_uni <- rd("unidim"); fit_two <- rd("twolex")
```

# The answer, read straight off the full model

```{r}
fit_full$summary(c("lambda_g", "sigma_s", "sigma_admin", "rho", "ecv",
                   "beta_exp", "beta_age", "beta_age_exp",
                   "sigma_concept", "sigma_delta"))

as_draws_df(fit_full$draws(c("rho", "ecv"))) |>
  pivot_longer(c(rho, ecv)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       title = "Posterior: correlation of the two language abilities, and person-level ECV")
```

- `rho` near 1 and `ecv` near 1 ⇒ **unidimensional**: one general trait,
  languages differ only by exposure-driven level.
- `rho` clearly below ~.7, `sigma_s` away from 0 ⇒ **separable lexicons**.
- Intermediate `ecv` (~.6–.85) ⇒ strong common trait **plus** non-trivial
  language-specific ability — report the number, don't binarise.

# Model comparison (LOO), as a cross-check

```{r}
loo_compare(list(
  full   = fit_full$loo(),
  unidim = fit_uni$loo(),
  twolex = fit_two$loo()
))
```

If `unidim` is within ~2 SE of `full`, the language-specific factors aren't
earning their keep. If `full` clearly beats both, general + specific is the right
description.

# Robustness

- **Age.** Re-fit within 6-month age bands (drop `beta_age*`), confirm
  `rho` / `ecv` are stable.
- **Concept linking.** Compare to `link_concepts: false` — if `rho` drops a lot,
  translation-equivalent structure is doing real work (conceptual vs lexical
  representation).
- **NUTS vs Pathfinder.** Iterate with `method: "pathfinder"` but report the NUTS
  fit — VI understates `sigma_s` uncertainty, the parameter in question.
- Feed `theta_child[,1]` / `theta_child[,2]` into `02_exposure_models.qmd` as a
  consistency check against the two-stage pipeline.

# SBC calibration (answers `10`'s open question)

One-rep-per-condition recovery check: simulate CDI responses from a **known**
`rho_true`, using the real EN–SP form design / age / exposure and empirical item
difficulties (from marginal endorsement rates) + discriminations drawn to match
the fitted `sigma_logalpha` (~0.27), then refit the full model.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# models/o5_bayes_SBC_calibration.csv
#  rho_true  rho_hat_median   95% CI            covers?
#      0.30      0.279       [0.191, 0.364]        yes
#      0.60      0.576       [0.512, 0.636]        yes
#      0.90      0.882       [0.858, 0.902]        yes  (Rhat 1.01, weaker ESS)
```

Recovery is good across the range, with a small (~0.02) low-side bias and no
systematic inflation. **This means the headline `rho`/`ecv` numbers below can be
read at face value** — the earlier worry (carried over from the mirt route in
`08`, which *does* overstate multidimensionality-adjacent quantities) does not
transfer to this Stan model.

# Cross-pair replication

| pair | children | items | `rho` (median, 95% CI) | `ecv` | divergences |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| English (American) × Spanish (Mexican) — **latest administration, own age (corrected)** | 474 | 543 | **0.399 [0.322, 0.473]** | 0.398 | 0 |
| English (American) × Spanish (Mexican) — collapsed visits *(superseded)* | 474 | 554 | 0.585 [0.519, 0.642] | 0.582 | 0 |
| English (American) × Spanish (Mexican) — collapsed visits, full 1665 items, concept linking on *(superseded)* | 474 | 1665 | 0.587 [0.528, 0.644] | 0.584 | 0 |
| English (British) × Spanish (European) — new pipeline | 690 | 417 | **0.698 [0.652, 0.738]** | 0.695 | 0 |
| English (British) × Spanish (European) — old pipeline, linear age *(superseded)* | 690 | ~420 | 0.708 [0.664, 0.747] | 0.706 | 0 |
| Norwegian × Polish — new pipeline | 112 | 697 | **0.563 [0.407, 0.686]** | 0.553 | 0 |
| Norwegian × Polish — old pipeline *(superseded)* | 112 | 697 | 0.593 [0.428, 0.709] | 0.586 | 0 |

All land between 0.4 and 0.7 — decisively **rejecting both** `rho → 1`
(unidimensional) **and** `rho → 0` (separable lexicons). Robustness (on the
pre-correction data): the full 1665-item EN-American × ES-Mexican fit (46 h,
translation-equivalent concept linking enabled) gave the same `rho` as the
554-item thinned run — item thinning and concept linking don't move it.
**Norwegian × Polish** (Germanic + Slavic, no English, a different bilingual
population) sits at 0.56, between the two English–Spanish estimates (wide
interval: n = 112). The two English–Spanish samples now differ clearly (0.40
vs. 0.70): the British/European sample has the higher CDI floor (10–13% of
children below 5 words vs. 3–5% elsewhere), the American/Mexican one the wider,
longitudinal age range. Which of these drives the gap is unresolved. The
British/European and Norwegian–Polish samples are effectively cross-sectional;
refit with the new pipeline (`scripts/fit_dim_irt.R latest 2 ...`) they move by
≤ 0.03. Saved: `models/o5_bayes_ENGB-ESEU-latest-thin2_summary.csv`,
`models/o5_bayes_NO-PL-latest-thin2_summary.csv`.

The Malaysian English/Malay/Mandarin trilingual sample (n=569) was fit with the
`L`-generalised model but the result — near-zero `rho` across all three pairs —
is an **artifact of CDI floor effects** (54% / 35% / 86% of children below 5
words in English / Malay / Mandarin; Mandarin exposure known for only 22%).
`sample_health()` flags this, and `build_pair_matrix()` now warns automatically.
No usable multilingual (3+) sample exists in the current export. See
`dimensionality_writeup.md`.

Saved: `models/o5_bayes_ENGB-ESEU_summary.csv`, `models/o5_bayes_NO-PL_summary.csv`,
`models/o5_bayes_SBC_calibration.csv`.
